title: Blowing up a commutator fixed scheme strictly reduces nonabelian inertia
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular separated scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth] with a tame generically free action of a finite group $G$, and let $\bar x$ be a geometric point whose inertia group $H\leq G$ is nonabelian. Set $K=[H,H]$, the subgroup generated by commutators $aba^{-1}b^{-1}$. Let $X^K$ be the closed subscheme equalizing every element of $K$ with the identity. The action of $H$ lifts to $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{X^K}X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], and for every geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$ above $\bar x$ its inertia subgroup in $H$ is a proper subgroup of $H$. In particular, if $p:W\to X$ is a maximally dominating $H$-equivariant morphism from a normal scheme such that the ideal of $X^K$ becomes an invertible ideal on $W$, then $p$ factors uniquely through $Y$, equivariantly for $H$, and every geometric inertia in $H$ above $\bar x$ is proper. Maximally dominating means taking generic points to generic points.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.8 and its normal-representation proof, printed p.79; used in VIII 4.2.13, printed p.122 (the reference there to VI 4.7 is the setup of Proposition 4.8). The factorization clause is VIII 2.2.4(i) and 4.2.13.

proof.text: Write $Z=X^K$, $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Z)$, and $b:Y\to X$ for the blowup map. The closed-immersion ideal is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; on Noetherian affine opens its ideals are finitely generated. Conjugation carries the equalizer equations for $K$ to those for $hKh^{-1}=K$, since a conjugate of a commutator is a commutator. Hence $H$ preserves $Z$ and $\mathcal I$. Let $x$ be the image of $\bar x$ and $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $k$. Each $h\in H$ fixes $x$ and acts trivially on $k$, since it fixes the geometric point. Use inverse pullback for the left action on $A$. The stalk $J=\mathcal I_x$ is the ideal generated by $u(a)-a$, $u\in K$, $a\in A$: pulling the diagonal equations $a\otimes1-1\otimes a$ back by $(u,1)$ gives these differences. Germs suffice here, since each of finitely many equations is represented on a common neighbourhood of $x$. In particular $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$.

source.place: VI 4.1 and Proposition 4.2, printed pp.76--77: fixed ideal as differences; VI Proposition 4.8, printed p.79: commutator subgroup

proof.text: By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], $\mathcal L=\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$ is an invertible ideal. For $h\in H$, the extended ideal along $h\circ b$ is the same ideal, because $h$ preserves $\mathcal I$. The final-object property [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] therefore gives a unique map $\widetilde h:Y\to Y$ with $b\widetilde h=hb$. Both $\widetilde h\widetilde{h'}$ and $\widetilde{hh'}$ lie over $hh'b$ and induce the same extended ideal, so uniqueness makes them equal. Likewise $\widetilde1=1$ and $\widetilde{h^{-1}}=\widetilde h^{-1}$. This is the asserted lifted action. Since it preserves the actual subsheaf $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$, the action also gives the canonical action on this invertible ideal, compatible with multiplication from $b^*\mathcal I$.

Consider the $k$-vector space $E=J/\mathfrak mJ$. The actions of $H$ on $J$ and $A$ induce a $k$-linear action on $E$, since $H$ is inertia. Tameness says that $|H|$ is invertible in $k$; hence $n=|K|$ is invertible too. Define $P=n^{-1}\sum_{v\in K}v$ on $E$. The vectors $e_{u,a}=[u(a)-a]$ span $E$ by Step 1. For each generator,
$$P(e_{u,a})=n^{-1}\left[\sum_{v\in K}(vu)(a)-\sum_{v\in K}v(a)\right]=0,$$
because $v\mapsto vu$ permutes $K$. Thus $P=0$. For every field extension $\Omega/k$, the same formula gives $P=0$ on $E\otimes_k\Omega$. In particular, if $q:E\otimes_k\Omega\to V$ is $K$-equivariant and $K$ acts trivially on $V$, then $q(Pe)=n^{-1}\sum_v q(ve)=q(e)$, so $q=0$. This is the explicit averaging calculation dual to the absence of invariant normal vectors in the source.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.8, printed p.79, last paragraph; agent-written conormal-quotient version of the normal-representation argument

proof.text:
Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ lie above $\bar x$, and suppose its inertia in $H$ were all of $H$. The fibre $L=\bar y^*\mathcal L$ is then a one-dimensional $\Omega$-vector space with a linear $H$-action. There is a canonical $H$-equivariant surjection
$$q:(J/\mathfrak mJ)\otimes_k\Omega\twoheadrightarrow L.$$
Indeed, the extended ideal is generated by images of local sections of $\mathcal I$, by [def-nagata-extended-ideal]; in a trivialization of the invertible ideal, these images generate its rank-one stalk, so their reductions generate its fibre. The map kills $\mathfrak mJ$ because $\mathfrak m$ maps to zero at $\bar y$. On a one-dimensional space every element of $H$ acts by a nonzero scalar, so its action is a character $H\to\Omega^\times$. Scalars commute, hence every $aba^{-1}b^{-1}$, and therefore $K$, acts trivially on $L$. Step 3 forces $q=0$, contradicting its surjectivity onto the nonzero space $L$. Consequently the inertia at every $\bar y$ is proper in $H$.

source.place: VI Proposition 4.8, printed p.79; dual version using the invertible exceptional ideal rather than lines in the normal bundle

proof.text: Now let $p:W\to X$ satisfy the stated hypotheses. Its extended ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_W$ is invertible by assumption. Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-universal-property] to obtain the unique $r:W\to Y$ with $br=p$. For each $h\in H$, the maps $r\circ h_W$ and $\widetilde h\circ r$ both lie over $h_X\circ p$; the extended ideal along that map is still invertible. Uniqueness in the same universal property gives $r h_W=\widetilde h r$. Thus $r$ is $H$-equivariant. Normality and maximal domination are allowed extra hypotheses here: the ordinary blowup universal property only needs the invertibility already assumed.

source.place: Tag 0806 (lemma-universal-property-blowing-up); ILO VIII 4.2.13, printed p.122, factorization through the ordinary commutator-fixed blowup

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar w$ of $W$ above $\bar x$, put $\bar y=r\bar w$. If $h\in H$ fixes $\bar w$ as a geometric point, then equivariance gives $\widetilde h\bar y=r h_W\bar w=r\bar w=\bar y$. Therefore $H_{\bar w}\leq H_{\bar y}<H$ by Step 4. A subgroup contained in a proper subgroup is proper. This proves the last inertia assertion, including when a fibre is empty, when the corresponding assertion has no points to check.

source.place: VIII 4.2.13, printed p.122: passage of strict inertia decrease through the equivariant factorization

Sources: ILO VI 4.1, 4.2 and 4.7, and Prop 4.8 on p.79 (normal-line character argument); VIII 4.2.13 on p.122 (factorization via the blowup universal property). Step 1: the stalk J is generated by u(a)-a, obtained by pulling back the diagonal ideal along (u,1); fractions handled; J lies in m. Step 2: H preserves I, so the lift exists and the group laws hold by uniqueness in the universal property (statement as in its blueprint_update); principalization supplies the invertible extended ideal. Step 3: P = n^{-1} sum of v over K vanishes on the spanning classes because v -> vu permutes K, so E^K = 0. Step 4: pulling back b^*I -> L along y gives a surjection E⊗Ω onto the 1-dimensional fibre L; H acts on L by a character, so K acts trivially, which contradicts Step 3. This is the honest dual of VI 4.8. Steps 5 and 6: uniqueness gives r∘h_W = h̃∘r, and H_w ≤ H_y < H. Checked cases: H abelian or J=0 (empty blowup, vacuous); D_n with n>2 from VI 4.6(b), where s swaps the two r-eigenlines; char dividing |K| shows where tameness is used. Duplicates: only the parent cites VI 4.8; the parent's Step 4 uses exactly the factorization and inertia-drop clauses. The seven declared generic tool uses are accepted; no SGA source.
